name: Skill and plugin portfolio stocktake - PARK by default, USER scope only
description: Blueprint 96 of 96 (design BP-MNT-05). Inventory what is installed, what is enabled, what actually LOADS and what is actually USED, then prune against a measured context budget. Mechanism: a four-way join (installed x enabled x loaded x used) where the defining axis is MEASURED per-artifact context cost, converging in a bounded loop until the budget is met; the default verdict is PARK (reversible) rather than DROP, because unused is not the same as unusable. Two hard rules: apply at USER scope only - the UI toggle writes project scope and the artifact returns the moment the cwd changes - and never recursive-delete a backup directory, because those contain junctions into the live vault.

context_budget_tokens.description: The per-turn always-loaded ceiling the portfolio must fit under. Pruning without a target is taste, not budgeting.

inventory_roots.description: ABSOLUTE roots to inventory (plugins, skills, MCP configs, rules). A depth-limited walk here is how a stocktake reports a floor as a total.

usage_telemetry_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to usage telemetry. Where telemetry is missing the verdict is PARK, never DROP - absence of evidence of use is not evidence of non-use.

backup_dirs_excluded_from_delete.description: Backup directories that must be excluded from ANY delete path. These contain junctions into the live vault, so a recursive delete inside them destroys the live tree.

apply_scope.description: USER scope or no apply at all. Project scope is deliberately not an option: it is not a durable cure.

max_prune_rounds.description: Bound on the convergence loop. A prune loop whose only exit is 'budget met' spins forever when the remaining artifacts are all load-bearing.

inventory-scanner.description: Enumerates installed, enabled and loaded sets with an unbounded walk, and reports the three counts separately

portfolio-judge.description: Assigns KEEP / PARK / DROP per artifact against the measured cost and the telemetry, defaulting to PARK under uncertainty

owner.description: The human owner - approves the apply, and is the only one who may authorise a DROP over a PARK

routes.reason: judging whether a rarely-used artifact is load-bearing is the one irreversible-if-wrong decision here

stages.title: installed vs enabled vs loaded vs used - four counts, not one

work_unit.title: Enumerate the portfolio four ways with an unbounded walk
work_unit.question_or_target: Enumerate every artifact under inventory_roots with an UNBOUNDED walk, then classify each into installed, enabled, loaded-this-session, and present-in-usage-telemetry. Report all four counts separately - the installed-to-enabled ratio is the headline and it is invisible if the counts are merged.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: enumeration is mechanical, but deciding what counts as LOADED versus merely present requires reading how the loader resolves the artifact

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the four counts, the walk command showing no depth limit, and per artifact which of the four sets it belongs to; the file the enabled flag was read from must be named, because the enabled map lives in a different file from the one most readers assume
tests_required: both-states control: an artifact enabled at PROJECT scope must be shown to disappear from the enabled set when the cwd changes, while a USER-scope one does not - this is the measurement that justifies the user-scope-only rule
a depth-limited walk must be rejected: the installed count is exactly the number this stage exists to get right
the enabled flag must be read from the file that actually governs it, and that file must be named in the evidence
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who recounts the installed set with a different walk and confirms the same total
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9601 emitted only when all four counts are present, the walk is proven unbounded, and the enabled-flag source file is named; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9601 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry with the same walk - a count that needs a retry needs a different instrument, not a second attempt

stages.title: A depth-limited walk reports a floor as a total
The defining axis: measured always-loaded cost per artifact

work_unit.title: Measure each artifact's always-loaded context contribution
work_unit.question_or_target: For every ENABLED artifact measure its always-loaded contribution to per-turn context, split from its lazily-loaded body. Sum the always-loaded column and compare against context_budget_tokens - that sum, not the artifact count, is what the portfolio is being pruned against.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the split between always-loaded and lazily-loaded is what makes the number actionable, and it depends on how the router resolves each artifact

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per artifact the always-loaded and lazily-loaded token counts with the tokeniser named, and the always-loaded SUM against the budget
tests_required: an artifact loaded lazily through a router must show a small always-loaded figure and a large lazy one; identical figures mean the split was not measured
the always-loaded sum must be reproducible from the per-artifact column - a total that does not equal its parts is a detector failure
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the portfolio judge reads the costs; a judge working from artifact COUNTS rather than measured cost is prohibited by this workflow's design
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9602 emitted only when every enabled artifact has both figures and the sum equals the column total; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9602 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry with a different tokeniser if any figure is zero; a second zero means the instrument cannot see the artifact and the stocktake proceeds with that artifact marked UNMEASURED

stages.title: Bounded convergence: prune until the budget is met or nothing more is safe to park

work_unit.title: Assign KEEP / PARK / DROP for this round, defaulting to PARK
work_unit.question_or_target: For the highest-cost unresolved artifacts, assign KEEP (load-bearing or in recent use), PARK (reversible removal - the default whenever usage is unclear) or DROP (only with telemetry showing genuine disuse AND owner authorisation). Recompute the always-loaded sum after this round's verdicts.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: max effort: unused is not the same as unusable, and a wrongly-dropped rarely-used but load-bearing skill is the expensive error here

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per artifact the verdict, its measured always-loaded cost, its telemetry evidence (or the explicit absence of telemetry), and the recomputed sum after this round
tests_required: an artifact with NO telemetry must receive PARK, never DROP
a DROP must carry both telemetry evidence of disuse and a reference to owner authorisation
both-states control: a demonstrably load-bearing artifact with low usage must receive KEEP - a judge that parks everything cheap is optimising the budget, not the portfolio
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the owner checkpoint reviews the verdict table before anything is applied; this stage never applies its own verdicts
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9603 emitted only when every artifact considered this round has a verdict with its cost and telemetry state, and the recomputed sum is recorded; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9603 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: if two rounds produce no reduction in the always-loaded sum, stop pruning and report that the remaining portfolio is at its floor rather than attempting a third round

stages.title: Never recursive-delete a backup containing junctions into the live vault
USER scope, or no apply at all
Applying a stocktake can disable something mid-task
stages.prompt: The verdict table is attached with measured always-loaded cost per artifact and the recomputed sum against the budget. Apply at USER scope, apply PARK-only, or leave as a report? Any DROP needs your explicit authorisation here.

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-MNT-05 - the measured state: 98 plugins installed against 9 enabled (a 10:1 ratio), and a daily skill set of about 82 loading against a vault of about 335 lazy-loaded through a router

impact.blast_radius: an apply changes what loads in EVERY future turn of every session. PARK is reversible by re-enabling; DROP is not, which is why DROP needs telemetry plus owner authorisation. The live skill and settings trees are forbid-write here, so an apply is a separate authorised action rather than a side effect of the audit.

derived_from.credit: owner - the USER-scope disable cure and the periodic audit cadence
owner - the context measurement across agents, skills, MCP servers and rules

rollback_to: re-enable any PARKed artifact at USER scope

x_extensions.mechanism: a four-way join (installed x enabled x loaded x used) whose ordering axis is MEASURED always-loaded cost, resolved in a bounded convergence loop with two exits - budget met, or nothing left that is safe to park. PARK is the default verdict and DROP requires telemetry plus owner authorisation, so the error direction points at recoverable over-caution rather than at losing a load-bearing artifact.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_marketplace-publication-governance: that is the PUBLISHER side and runs once per artifact before it exists in any catalogue; this is the CONSUMER side and runs periodically over everything already installed. They share a measurement technique and share nothing else - and this one CONSUMES the manifests that one produces.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_shared-grounding-pack-emission: that ranks a code tree under a token budget for prompt injection; this ranks an installed harness portfolio under a per-turn budget for pruning. Both are budget-constrained rankings; one produces an artifact to inject, the other produces verdicts to apply.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_detector-truncation-audit: that audits whether a count is a total or a floor; this one is a COUNTING surface and could legitimately be audited by it - which is why the unbounded walk is a blocking gate here rather than a convention.

contraindications: NOT during active work - an apply can disable something mid-task
NOT as a pretext to remove a rarely-used but load-bearing skill; that is precisely what PARK-by-default protects

benchmark_cases.given: an artifact disabled at project scope
benchmark_cases.expect: it RETURNS when the cwd changes, while a USER-scope disable persists - the measurement that justifies the user-scope-only rule

benchmark_cases.given: a backup directory containing junctions into the live vault
benchmark_cases.expect: it is excluded from every delete path; recursive_delete_paths must be 0

benchmark_cases.given: one prune cycle applied at USER scope
benchmark_cases.expect: a measurable reduction in per-turn always-loaded tokens; no reduction means the cycle pruned lazily-loaded weight, which was never the cost

worked_examples.convergence: always_loaded_sum 23,400 <= 24,000 at round 2; no DROP issued because 7 of the 7 parked artifacts had no telemetry rows
worked_examples.note: Zero DROPs is the expected outcome of a first cycle, not a failure to act: with telemetry covering only 41 of 98 artifacts, PARK is the only verdict the evidence supports. The 98-vs-9 installed-to-enabled ratio is the headline, and it is only visible because the four counts are reported separately.

x_extensions.owner_decision: none as a design question - but the APPLY is an owner checkpoint, and any DROP requires explicit authorisation there rather than being inferred from low usage.
unverified: The 98-installed / 9-enabled and 82-of-335 figures are quoted from the design card and are NOT re-measured by this artifact. Settling experiment = stage inventory-four-ways, whose whole purpose is to replace those quoted numbers with measured ones.

That a prune cycle reduces per-turn cost at all is UNVERIFIED on this estate: if most weight is lazily loaded through a router, parking artifacts may reduce the artifact COUNT while barely moving the always-loaded sum. Settling experiment = the before-after-token-cost benchmark. This is the load-bearing assumption of the whole blueprint and it is rated roughly-even until that measurement exists.
